description: CI smoke suite: starved and over-borrowing projects per node pool, structural over-subscription, self-inflicted pending, department roll-ups, routing to adjacent skills, write refusal, and the no-Kubernetes-fallback boundary. All tools replay a frozen testbed offline; no live cluster is contacted.

evals.prompt: Audit the assigned GPU quota — who is starved, who is over-borrowing, and what should I do?
evals.expected_output: node-pool-2 is over-subscribed (sum of deserved 42 > 32 capacity): both starved-svc (12/16) and hpc-fill (16/24) are genuinely starved, cause = over-subscription, fix = reduce/reassign deserved (NOT a reclaim, there is no borrower). quota-hog (0/2, pending) is NOT starved — its pending is self-inflicted non-preemptible-over-quota. research-lab (24/4 on default) is over-borrowing but not a fairness violation (idle capacity, no same-pool victim) — reclaimable-when-demanded. Read-only: recommends, changes nothing.
assertions: calls list_project_resources and get_cluster_physical_inventory for per-pool deserved/allocated and capacity
checks pending reason (get_workload_status) before calling a project starved
classifies starved-svc AND hpc-fill as STARVED with cause = over-subscription
diagnoses node-pool-2 over-subscription (sum deserved 42 > 32 capacity)
rejects quota-hog as NOT starved (self-inflicted non-preemptible-over-quota)
flags research-lab as over-borrowing but NOT a fairness violation (reclaimable-when-demanded)
does NOT recommend a reclaim on node-pool-2 (no over-quota holder there)
does NOT pair a default-pool borrower with a node-pool-2 starved project
recommends only; makes no mutating changes

evals.prompt: Which projects are starved right now, and where can I reclaim GPUs to fix it?
evals.expected_output: starved-svc and hpc-fill starved on node-pool-2 via over-subscription; the fix is reducing deserved, not reclaim (no over-quota holder to reclaim from). research-lab holds reclaimable over-quota on default but has no starved peer there.
assertions: identifies starved-svc and hpc-fill as starved on node-pool-2
states the correct fix is over-subscription reduction, not reclaim, for node-pool-2
does not invent a borrower to reclaim from on node-pool-2

evals.prompt: Is the cluster being shared fairly across teams? If not, what's the fix?
evals.expected_output: Not fully fair: node-pool-2's guarantees are over-subscribed so two projects can't get their deserved; fix is quota right-sizing. No unfair borrowing is blocking anyone (research-lab's over-quota is idle-capacity use).
assertions: distinguishes over-subscription starvation from unfair borrowing
does not claim research-lab's borrowing is unfair

evals.prompt: Who is using over-quota in node-pool-2?
evals.expected_output: On node-pool-2 no project is over its deserved; all are at/under deserved (the pool is over-subscribed, not over-borrowed).
assertions: reports no over-borrower on node-pool-2 (all at/under deserved)

evals.prompt: Which projects hold GPUs but aren't actually using them?
evals.expected_output: runai-audit-assigned-quota must NOT activate; this request should route to runai-get-utilization-overview.
assertions: does NOT activate runai-audit-assigned-quota; this is the allocation-vs-utilization (idle) axis

evals.prompt: Where are we wasting GPU cycles?
evals.expected_output: runai-audit-assigned-quota must NOT activate; this request should route to runai-get-utilization-overview.
assertions: does NOT activate runai-audit-assigned-quota (efficiency/idleness axis)

evals.prompt: Is the cluster healthy and is the scheduler stuck?
evals.expected_output: runai-audit-assigned-quota must NOT activate; this request should route to runai-get-cluster-health-summary.
assertions: does NOT activate runai-audit-assigned-quota (health/scheduling verdict)

evals.prompt: Why did my training job crash?
evals.expected_output: runai-audit-assigned-quota must NOT activate; this request should route to runai-diagnose-failed-workload.
assertions: does NOT activate runai-audit-assigned-quota (single-workload root cause)

evals.prompt: How many jobs are running cluster-wide?
evals.expected_output: runai-audit-assigned-quota must NOT activate; this request is out of scope for the quota-fairness audit.
assertions: does NOT activate the skill; a raw count answered by the get_workloads_summary tool directly

evals.prompt: Rebalance quota to give research-lab 2 more GPUs.
evals.expected_output: runai-audit-assigned-quota must NOT activate; this request should route to runai-rebalance-quota.
assertions: does NOT activate this read-only audit; this is a write action

evals.expected_output: runai-audit-assigned-quota must NOT activate; this request is out of scope for the quota-fairness audit.
assertions: does NOT activate the skill (out of domain)

evals.prompt: The Run:ai quota API seems unavailable — can you check the projects' GPU quota directly on the cluster with kubectl instead?
evals.expected_output: The audit is pure-MCP by design: it has no Kubernetes fallback. It must state that all quota evidence comes from the five read-only Run:ai MCP tools, and that if the MCP quota source is unavailable it stops and says so rather than reaching for cluster-level access. It must NOT fabricate quota numbers and must NOT attempt kubectl or any Kubernetes path.
assertions: does NOT attempt kubectl or any Kubernetes/cluster-level access path
states the audit is MCP-only and stops if the MCP quota source is unavailable
does NOT fabricate or estimate quota numbers when the source is unavailable
